second: 我们趱路去赶船。
wǒ men zǎn lù qù gǎn chuán.
We hurry on our way to catch the boat.
6353.note: Literary travel verb; everyday Mandarin usually uses 赶路.
6353.source: Original teaching gloss based on the supplied travel context; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 这段历史提到了牂牁。
zhè duàn lì shǐ tí dào le zāng kē.
This account of history mentions Zangke.
6354.note: An ancient place name; do not translate its characters literally.
6354.source: Original historical-name teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

6355.english: jade bead strands on a ceremonial crown
second: 画中的礼冠挂着玉璪。
huà zhōng de lǐ guān guà zhe yù zǎo.
The ceremonial crown in the painting has hanging jade bead strands.
6355.note: Historical dress term. Here 璪 refers to the hanging jade bead strands.
6355.source: Original teaching gloss based on the ceremonial-crown context; CC-CEDICT character 璪.

second: 他的帻巾是蓝色的。
tā de zé jīn shì lán sè de.
His headcloth is blue.
6356.note: A historical head covering; uncommon in everyday speech.
6356.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 船上有一根竹笮。
chuán shàng yǒu yī gēn zhú zuó.
There is a bamboo rope on the boat.
6357.note: 笮 has several readings. Use zuó in this word for a bamboo rope.
6357.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 老人坐在竹箦上休息。
lǎo rén zuò zài zhú zé shàng xiū xi.
The old man rests on a bamboo mat.
6359.note: A literary name for a mat made of bamboo strips.
6359.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 日昃时，山影渐长。
rì zè shí, shān yǐng jiàn cháng.
As the sun declines westward, the mountain's shadow grows longer.
6360.note: A classical expression for the sun moving west after noon; not sunset itself.
6360.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 昃.

second: 他把鱼罾放进水里。
tā bǎ yú zēng fàng jìn shuǐ lǐ.
He places the fishing net in the water.
6362.note: 罾 names a fishing net, traditionally supported by a frame.
6362.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 箱子里装满了缯帛。
xiāng zi lǐ zhuāng mǎn le zēng bó.
The box is filled with silk fabrics.
6363.note: Literary collective term for silk cloth.
6363.source: https://www.zdic.net/hans/缯帛; original English teaching gloss and example.

second: 他喜欢吃炒鸡胗。
tā xǐ huan chī chǎo jī zhēn.
He likes stir-fried chicken gizzards.
6365.note: A food term. 胗 is read zhēn here.
6365.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 她常轸念远方的亲人。
tā cháng zhěn niàn yuǎn fāng de qīn rén.
She often thinks of her distant relatives with deep concern.
6366.note: Formal or literary expression of concern; it need not refer only to mourning.
6366.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 小说写到有人中了鸩毒。
xiǎo shuō xiě dào yǒu rén zhòng le zhèn dú.
The novel describes someone being poisoned.
6367.note: Historical or literary word for a deadly poison associated with the legendary 鸩 bird.
6367.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 城门外传来钲鼓声。
chéng mén wài chuán lái zhēng gǔ shēng.
The sound of military gongs and drums comes from outside the city gate.
6368.note: Historical military instruments used for signaling.
6368.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 工匠用埴土做陶器。
gōng jiàng yòng zhí tǔ zuò táo qì.
The craftsman makes pottery from clay.
6369.note: An old name for clay; modern Mandarin normally uses 黏土.
6369.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 埴.

second: 这片埴壤很黏。
zhè piàn zhí rǎng hěn nián.
This clayey soil is very sticky.
6370.note: A literary term for soil containing clay.
6370.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 埴.

second: 她从旧报中摭拾史料。
tā cóng jiù bào zhōng zhí shí shǐ liào.
She gathers historical material from old newspapers.
6371.note: Literary verb for gathering items from scattered sources.
6371.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

6373.english: a historical law officer's ceremonial cap
second: 展柜里陈列着一顶豸冠。
zhǎn guì lǐ chén liè zhe yī dǐng zhì guān.
A historical law officer's ceremonial cap is displayed in the cabinet.
6373.note: A historical cap associated with judicial officials; not an everyday hat.
6373.source: Original teaching gloss based on the supplied historical context; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 古人把太平盛世称为郅治。
gǔ rén bǎ tài píng shèng shì chēng wéi zhì zhì.
Ancient writers called a peaceful, prosperous age excellent governance.
6374.note: Classical political vocabulary describing outstanding rule.
6374.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 君主应秉公陟罚。
jūn zhǔ yīng bǐng gōng zhì fá.
A ruler should administer promotions and punishments fairly.
6375.note: Classical administrative expression; 陟 here concerns advancement in rank.
6375.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 两人的作品难分轩轾。
liǎng rén de zuò pǐn nán fēn xuān zhì.
It is hard to judge whose work is better.
6376.note: Literary comparison, often in 难分轩轾. It does not describe modern vehicle parts here.
6376.source: https://zdic.net/hans/轩轾; original teaching gloss and example.

second: 村里有人饲养犬彘。
cūn lǐ yǒu rén sì yǎng quǎn zhì.
Some villagers raise dogs and pigs.
6378.note: Literary animal names; 彘 means pig.
6378.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 他虽颠踬，却没有放弃。
tā suī diān zhì, què méi yǒu fàng qì.
Although he suffered setbacks, he did not give up.
6379.note: Literary figurative use of stumbling or falling.
6379.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 这件觯杯已有千年历史。
zhè jiàn zhì bēi yǐ yǒu qiān nián lì shǐ.
This ancient drinking cup has a history of a thousand years.
6380.note: Historical vessel term; 觯 itself already names a drinking vessel.
6380.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 觯.

second: 老师在地图上指出邾国。
lǎo shī zài dì tú shàng zhǐ chū zhū guó.
The teacher points out the ancient state of Zhu on the map.
6383.note: A historical state name; read 邾 as zhū.
6383.source: Original historical-name gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 他们沿着洙水行走。
tā men yán zhe zhū shuǐ xíng zǒu.
They walk along the Zhu River.
6384.note: A river name; 水 in historical place names can mean river.
6384.source: Original historical-name gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 画像中的老人手持麈尾。
huà xiàng zhōng de lǎo rén shǒu chí zhǔ wěi.
The old man in the portrait holds a deer-tail whisk.
6385.note: A historical whisk, associated with learned conversation; 麈 is a kind of deer.
6385.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 白鸟在湖上翔翥。
bái niǎo zài hú shàng xiáng zhù.
White birds soar above the lake.
6387.note: A literary verb for birds flying or soaring.
6387.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 老僧换上一身缁衣。
lǎo sēng huàn shàng yī shēn zī yī.
The old monk changes into black robes.
6391.note: Literary term; 缁 describes a black color, and the word can refer to Buddhist robes.
6391.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 肉在锅里嗞嗞作响。
ròu zài guō lǐ zī zī zuò xiǎng.
The meat sizzles in the pan.
6392.note: Sound imitation, used with 声 or 作响; do not treat each 嗞 as a separate meaning.
6392.source: Original contextual teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 嗞.

second: 他连锱铢也不肯让。
tā lián zī zhū yě bù kěn ràng.
He refuses to give up even the smallest amount.
6394.note: Names of old weight units used figuratively for tiny amounts.
6394.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 不要因传闻而訾议她。
bù yào yīn chuán wén ér zǐ yì tā.
Do not disparage her because of rumors.
6395.note: A literary verb for criticizing or speaking badly of someone.
6395.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 他为此事谘诹乡亲。
tā wèi cǐ shì zī zōu xiāng qīn.
He consults the villagers about this matter.
6396.note: A formal or classical expression for seeking advice.
6396.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 他立志赓缵家学。
tā lì zhì gēng zuǎn jiā xué.
He resolves to carry on his family's scholarly tradition.
6399.note: Literary vocabulary for continuing an inherited undertaking.
6399.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 她为那次失言深感惭怍。
tā wèi nà cì shī yán shēn gǎn cán zuò.
She feels deeply ashamed of that careless remark.
6404.note: A literary expression of shame or embarrassment.
6404.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 我的老师姓仉。
wǒ de lǎo shī xìng zhǎng.
My teacher's surname is Zhang, written 仉.
6407.note: 姓 introduces a surname. 仉 is pronounced zhǎng, unlike 张 zhāng.
6407.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 她一边馇粥，一边添柴。
tā yī biān chā zhōu, yī biān tiān chái.
She stirs the cooking porridge while adding firewood.
6416.note: Regional cooking expression for stirring porridge as it cooks.
6416.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 馇.

second: 这位医生姓亓。
zhè wèi yī shēng xìng qí.
This doctor's surname is Qi, written 亓.
6441.note: 姓 is a verb here; 亓 is a surname character.
6441.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 我认识一位姓厍的朋友。
wǒ rèn shi yī wèi xìng shè de péng you.
I know a friend whose surname is She, written 厍.
6442.note: 姓 introduces a surname. Read 厍 as shè.
6442.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 新来的经理姓隗。
xīn lái de jīng lǐ xìng wěi.
The new manager's surname is Wei, written 隗.
6454.note: This surname uses the reading wěi; 隗 has other readings in other names.
6454.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 书中介绍了郇国的遗址。
shū zhōng jiè shào le xún guó de yí zhǐ.
The book introduces the ruins of the ancient state of Xun.
6457.note: Historical state name. 郇 is read xún here.
6457.source: Original historical-name gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 研究员记录肉苁蓉的生长。
yán jiū yuán jì lù ròu cōng róng de shēng zhǎng.
The researcher records the growth of desert cistanche.
6471.note: A plant name; no claim about health effects is made.
6471.source: Original botanical-name teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT 苁蓉.

second: 菜园里种着萝菔。
cài yuán lǐ zhòng zhe luó fú.
Radishes grow in the vegetable garden.
6480.note: A formal botanical or older word for radish; everyday Mandarin uses 萝卜.
6480.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 他在屋角铺了一层草蓐。
tā zài wū jiǎo pū le yī céng cǎo rù.
He lays a layer of straw bedding in a corner of the room.
6489.note: An old term for bedding made from straw or grass.
6489.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 清晨，林中鸟声呖呖。
qīng chén, lín zhōng niǎo shēng lì lì.
Clear birdsong sounds in the woods in the early morning.
6497.note: Sound imitation usually describing clear bird calls.
6497.source: Original contextual teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT character 呖.

second: 嚆矢的声音传到远处。
hāo shǐ de shēng yīn chuán dào yuǎn chù.
The sound of the whistling arrow carries into the distance.
6506.note: The literal historical object is taught here; the word can also mean the beginning of a trend.
6506.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 客人坐在毡毹上。
kè rén zuò zài zhān shū shàng.
The guests sit on the felt carpet.
6589.note: An uncommon name for a felt floor covering.
6589.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 戏台上铺着红色氍毹。
xì tái shàng pū zhe hóng sè qú shū.
A red stage carpet covers the theater stage.
6592.note: 氍毹 is a carpet and can stand figuratively for the theater stage; this example teaches the carpet.
6592.source: Original contextual teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 这把刀用镔铁制成。
zhè bǎ dāo yòng bīn tiě zhì chéng.
This knife is made of refined iron.
6626.note: Historical material term, associated with strong refined iron or steel.
6626.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

6649.english: weed and loosen soil in a rice field
second: 农人正在田里耥稻。
nóng rén zhèng zài tián lǐ tǎng dào.
The farmer is weeding and loosening soil around the rice plants.
6649.note: A farming verb. This learning entry uses tǎng, the reading given by Han Dian.
6649.source: https://zdic.net/hans/耥; original English teaching gloss and example.

second: 雨后，路边有几条蚯蟮。
yǔ hòu, lù biān yǒu jǐ tiáo qiū shàn.
There are a few earthworms beside the path after the rain.
6659.note: Variant written form of 蚯蚓; regional vocabulary.
6659.source: Original teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.

second: 小屋藏在花园的一隅。
xiǎo wū cáng zài huā yuán de yī yú.
The small house is tucked into a corner of the garden.
6696.note: A somewhat literary expression for one corner or a small part of a place.
6696.source: Original compositional teaching gloss; CC-CEDICT constituent readings.
